standard_prerequisites: the rig-smooth criterion via H^0 of the completed naively trivialized cotangent complex being locally finite projective and H^{-1} killed by a power of the ideal of definition
the long exact cohomology sequence from the transitivity triangle for NL
the annihilator lemmas for the two-term complex under base change
localization and extensions of finite projective modules
core_obligations: Prove that the composite of two rig-smooth continuous morphisms A to B and B to C of adic Noetherian rings is rig-smooth
proof_roadmap: Choose an ideal of definition I of A giving the topologies of B and C; the transitivity triangle for NL gives the six-term exact cohomology sequence relating NL_{C/A}, NL_{C/B} and NL_{B/A} base-changed to C
The degree -1 terms on the outside are annihilated by a power of I (rig-smoothness of the two factors plus the annihilator lemmas handling the base change), hence so is H^{-1}(NL_{C/A}^wedge)

The rig-smooth criterion provides f_i in IB and g_j in IC cutting out V(IB) and V(IC) with H^0(NL_{B/A})_{f_i} and H^0(NL_{C/B})_{g_j} finite projective; after localizing at f_i g_j the degree -1 terms vanish and the exact sequence becomes short exact
H^0(NL_{C/A})_{f_i g_j} is an extension of finite projective modules, hence finite projective; the criterion then gives that C is rig-smooth over (A,I)
difficulty_reason: H2: a homological-algebra composition argument with a localization bookkeeping step; the source writes out both exact sequences and every quoted criterion.
